The passage describes a group of people who are virtuous and upright. They do not turn to evil, but instead remain good. They do not use oaths, as they do not distrust or deceive others. They do not desire money or seek empty glory, instead referring all things to the glory of Christ.

The passage also criticizes a person named Luther, stating that he is inconsistent in his beliefs, as he says one thing at the beginning and something else later on, recanting what he said before. The author finds this inconsistency troubling. The author also mentions that the author of the Assertion (presumably Luther's writing) may have been put off by something, although it is not specified what that might be.
